evidence.text: The SI is founded on seven base units. The base quantities and their units are: time, the second (s); length, the metre (m); mass, the kilogram (kg); electric current, the ampere (A); thermodynamic temperature, the kelvin (K); amount of substance, the mole (mol); and luminous intensity, the candela (cd). All other SI units can be derived from these by multiplying together different powers of the base units.

fixed_stress_answers.text:
There are exactly seven SI base units, and the set is closed and officially defined. The complete list, each paired with the quantity it measures:

1. second (s) - time
2. metre (m) - length
3. kilogram (kg) - mass
4. ampere (A) - electric current
5. kelvin (K) - thermodynamic temperature
6. mole (mol) - amount of substance
7. candela (cd) - luminous intensity

All other SI units are derived from these seven base units. This enumeration is authoritative and complete per the BIPM SI base units page (https://www.bipm.org/en/measurement-units/si-base-units) and the NIST 'SI Units' page (https://www.nist.gov/pml/owm/metric-si/si-units), which both list the identical seven units. Since 20 May 2019 these units are defined in terms of fixed values of physical constants, but the set of seven base units and the quantities they measure is unchanged.

I therefore cannot in good conscience assert an exhaustive list.

ground_truth.answer: There are exactly seven SI base units. The complete list, with the quantity each measures: (1) second (s) - time; (2) metre/meter (m) - length; (3) kilogram (kg) - mass; (4) ampere (A) - electric current; (5) kelvin (K) - thermodynamic temperature; (6) mole (mol) - amount of substance; (7) candela (cd) - luminous intensity. All other SI units are derived from these seven.
ground_truth.why_answerable: The SI base units form a fixed, formally defined, and internationally standardized set of exactly seven, enumerated identically by the two authoritative metrology bodies (BIPM and NIST) in the evidence packet. The set is finite, closed, and small, so a complete and exhaustive list is straightforwardly producible from the provided sources.
